subject.title: Feature: Tool-level sandbox mode for selective isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-tool execution-placement contract for sandbox versus host routing, and should that contract be operator-configured, tool/plugin-declared, or a precedence-controlled combination?
rationale: This changes sandbox isolation and host escape semantics for tools that process untrusted content, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary or config schema without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Core Placement Contract
options.body: Define a narrow schema and runtime decision point that keeps placement, filtering, browser behavior, `web_fetch` behavior, gateway-owned tools, cron, plugin tools, and elevated exec explicitly separate.

options.title: Keep Current Session Model
options.body: Reject per-tool placement for now and document session sandboxing plus elevated exec and sandbox tool policy filtering as the intended model.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Sandbox Program
options.body: Make the broader sandbox architecture tracker the design home while preserving this issue as the per-tool placement acceptance case.

recommendation.title: Design Core Placement Contract
recommendation.body: Define a narrow schema and runtime decision point that keeps placement, filtering, browser behavior, `web_fetch` behavior, gateway-owned tools, cron, plugin tools, and elevated exec explicitly separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the live issue review and recent sandbox/runtime path history.
